text:
liz: quick heads-up — prototyping a microbatching fastpath for the continuous scheduler. goal: cut p50 for short requests by avoiding full pooling delay. sketch below.
amar: curious — how is this different from the existing adaptive-window pooling? sounds like a fastpath is more opportunistic.
liz: right. pooling batches by time window adds a fixed delay. fastpath tries to pair incoming short requests with an in-flight batch if they're compatible (same model, compat quant, similar seq len). no wait if match found.
tara: risk: head-of-line fairness. if you always attach to in-flight big batches you might starve single-request tenants.
liz: agreed. thinking admission rules + per-tenant token budget. also a cap on how many attachments per batch.
mike: what about KV cache interactions? attaching mid-batch could miss cached KV and increase perf variance.
liz: good point — we only allow attachments when KV cache state is compatible (same prefix keyspace or empty). otherwise fall back to normal pooling.
amar: detail: how do we check compatibility cheaply? full key compare is expensive.
liz: plan: maintain a short fingerprint on batch prefix (rolling hash) and compare. cheap and probabilistic. collisions rare; fall back to normal path on mismatch.
tara: sounds reasonable. what metrics should we track to validate? p50/p95 per-tenant, attach_success_rate, batch_size_distribution, cache_hit_rate, unfairness_index.
mike: add "tail_attachment_latency" separate metric for attaches. also GPU kernel inefficiency metric if sequence len mismatch increases pad fraction.
liz: yep. experiment heuristic config I'm proposing:

```
fastpath: {
  enabled: true,
  max_attachments_per_batch: 4,
  max_seqlen_ratio: 1.2,   # don't attach if seqlen > 1.2*batch_avg
  fingerprint_threshold: 0.9
}
```

amar: we should A/B this at the tenant level. run 10% of tenants on fastpath with high-frequency short requests.
liz: exactly. experiment feel: 2 weeks, synthetic load + small set of prod tenants, rollbackable flag.
devrel-bot: perf-tests queued: https://ci.internal/reports/fastpath-proto-181200 — will post results when done :hourglass_flowing_sand:
mike: operational concerns: batch lifecycle changes might complicate tracing and billing (per-token charge attribution when attached mid-batch).
liz: billing note — attribute attached tokens to their request id; runtime will emit per-request token counts even if served in a shared kernel run.
tara: eviction interplay: if attached requests cause KV cache churn, we might increase downstream latency. need cache eviction budget per-batch.
amar: also consider fairness emergency throttle: if unfairness_index > threshold, disable fastpath for offending tenant for N minutes.
liz: good addition. implement counters: attaches_per_tenant_window and global_unfairness. config knobs for soft/hard limits.
mike: could also expose fastpath as a per-route feature flag so customers can opt in for latency-sensitive endpoints.
liz: yep — default off for now in prod. opt-in via routing policy.
devrel-bot: small demo artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-dev/fastpath/proto/attach-demo.log
ci-bot: smoke tests: attach + detach flows passed on x86 emu; failing on quantized kernels (investigating).
amar: next steps: 1) land experimental config + telemetry, 2) run small A/B, 3) collect metrics and kernel-level traces, 4) iterate on attach gating.
tara: I'd like a short doc on failure modes and rollback plan before we enable on any prod tenants.
liz: will draft that today and post in #eng-runtime. thanks all :thumbsup:
